Zelenskyy rejected the call during a wide-ranging briefing with reporters on Saturday.
“I believe that in a war like this, elections as such are a huge risk. Elections right now are a tsunami for the country that will split Ukraine,” the president said in comments published on Sunday.
“If we want to destroy the country, then we can move in the direction of elections during these times of war,” he added.
The 35-year-old Fedorov – a popular figure in Ukraine – held his post for just six months until Zelenskyy fired him in July, prompting protests across the country.
On Tuesday, he posted an explosive nine-minute video on YouTube claiming that Ukraine’s democracy “cannot be held hostage by Russia”.
“Can Russia actually be entitled to define when Ukrainians can elect their authorities next time? I’m sure it’s not,” he said, adding that Kyiv faces a “systemic crisis of governance”.
Experts have told Al Jazeera, however, that any wartime election would be practically impossible amid logistical and safety challenges, a reality that most Ukrainians agree with.
Kyiv tackles missile launchers, Starlink
Zelenskyy’s domestic political crisis is playing out as his government seeks more ways to curtail Moscow’s deadly air strikes.
Overnight Russian strikes in the eastern Donetsk region killed two people and wounded two others on Sunday, Ukraine’s emergency services said on Telegram. At least 141 private homes sustained damage in the attack.
Another eight people, including a child, were wounded in a drone attack on the northeastern city of Kharkiv that burned at least two residential buildings, the service said.
Meanwhile in the Odesa region, a Russian drone hit a passenger train travelling from Zhytomyr to Odesa, the Kyiv Independent reported, citing Ukrainian Railways CEO Oleksandr Pertsovskyi. No casualties were reported.
Amid the attacks, Zelenskyy said on Saturday that Ukraine is especially focused on hitting Russian ballistic launchers as Moscow ramps up its use of missiles – which effectively can only be destroyed by US-designed Patriot systems.
Ukraine has received just 264 Patriot missiles in 2026, down from 364 in 2025 and 675 in 2023, he said.
“When our antiballistic missiles are minimised – here is another tactic … hunting their nearby locations from which ballistic missiles are launched,” Zelenskyy said.
Ukraine is seeking to produce Patriot missiles domestically after receiving political blessing from United States President Donald Trump.
The Ukrainian president also said Moscow and Kyiv are building their own versions of Starlink, the satellite system used for battlefield communications that is controlled by US tech billionaire Elon Musk.
Russia’s alternative, developed “together with the Chinese”, is expected to be operational by December, Zelenskyy said.
He added that Ukraine would not “just sit and wait for Russia and China” and was “implementing a similar project with a European country”.
Funding gap
Ukraine’s wartime efforts may be hampered by a $27bn defence funding gap this year, Zelenskyy said, following defence spending that was higher than expected in the first half of 2026.
Ukraine needs at least $8bn for “a normal start” to 2027, he said, in addition to about $20bn more for other spending such as military salaries and payments to families of the dead.
Ukraine has reached an agreement with France for at least one SAMP/T air defence system this year, Zelenskyy said, and with Germany on the supply of about 600 PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors through 2028.
Norway said on Sunday it would give 85 billion crowns ($9.2bn) to Kyiv for the 2027 fiscal year, in line with what it provided in 2026.

articles.title: U.S. Unveils AIM-424 Malice: Ultra-Long-Range Missile With Range of Over 463 km
articles.body:
The U.S. Navy’s Naval Aviation branch has unveiled a new ultra-long-range air-to-air missile, the AIM-424 Malice, with a stated range of more than 463 km.
The relevant photographs were published by DVIDS, the official media platform of the U.S. Department of Defense.
The missile was shown on two types of carrier-based fighter aircraft: the F-35C Lightning II and the F/A-18E Super Hornet.
The missile was developed and manufactured by the U.S. company Raytheon. It is powered by a solid-propellant rocket motor.
The missile is 4.11 meters long, has a diameter of 0.34 meters, and a wingspan of 0.67 meters. Its launch mass is 680.4 kg. The missile has a stated range of more than 463 km and is equipped with a high-explosive fragmentation warhead.
Although photographs of the AIM-424 Malice were not released until August 22, 2026, available information indicates that testing of the missile began as early as the winter of 2026.
There is currently no detailed information regarding the completion of the missile’s integration with its carrier aircraft. However, the released photographs demonstrate that the F/A-18E Super Hornet can accommodate at least four AIM-424 Malice missiles.
The carrier-based F-35C can carry these missiles in its internal weapons bays, allowing the aircraft to maintain a low observable signature while conducting combat missions.
It is currently unknown what specific role the AIM-424 Malice will play in the U.S. Navy’s weapons inventory. The U.S. Air Force and U.S. Navy have traditionally developed their own air-launched missiles in parallel. Naval aviation already employs the AIM-120, while the U.S. Navy recently unveiled and test-fired the long-range AIM-174 during an exercise.
The AIM-424 Malice could potentially complement the AIM-174 or partially replace it.
In terms of design, the new missile more closely resembles conventional air-to-air missiles, whereas the AIM-174 was developed from the ship-launched SM-6 surface-to-air missile. The latter is also capable of intercepting ballistic targets, making it an important component in countering Chinese anti-ship ballistic missiles.
Meanwhile, the U.S. Air Force is developing its own long-range AIM-260 missile. It is likewise intended to engage targets at extended ranges. However, no official data on its range or other key performance characteristics have been released to date.

articles.body:
'Hunting their launch sites' — Zelensky reveals new details about Ukraine's ballistic missile defense
Ukraine has launched a new operation targeting Russian ballistic missile launchers near its borders, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Aug. 22, as Kyiv faces a shortage of missiles capable of intercepting ballistic weapons.
Zelensky said that Ukrainian military struck an Iskander ballistic missile launcher near Ukraine's borders on Aug. 22, without providing further details.
The strike was part of a separate operation to hunt down Russian missile systems positioned near Ukraine, which Zelensky described as an alternative tactic amid the dire lack of of anti-ballistic missile interceptors.
The Iskander is Russia's main surface to surface tactical ballistic missile system, with a stated range of around 500 kilometers.
Complemented with North Korean KN-23 ballistic missiles and advanced Zircon cruise missiles, the Iskander has been the workhorse of combined mass attacks again Ukrainian targets in recent months.
When attacking Kyiv and other targets inside Ukraine, Iskanders are launched from mobile erector-launcher systems inside Russian territory, usually in border regions like Bryansk or Kursk oblasts.
With Ukraine's stocks of Patriot ballistic missile interceptor at or near empty, strikes against Iskander launchers have long been proposed as an alternative method of fighting the Iskander threat, but Ukraine has lacked options for quickly detecting and hitting launch sites.
"At one point (the Russians) were planning to launch an attack, but didn’t go through with it. This is no coincidence," Zelensky told journalists.
"In other words, we're working to prevent them from carrying out large-scale missile attacks. These are individual, complex operations, and we're now starting to see the first results."
Zelensky said Russia could potentially produce up to 1,300 ballistic missiles annually and currently has around 600–630 in stock. Moscow could eventually aim to produce around 100 ballistic missiles per month, he said, although it has not yet reached that rate.
Ukraine is also seeking more Patriot interceptors ahead of winter, Zelensky said, revealing that Ukraine had only received 264 missiles for the advanced surface-to-air system this year so far.
The Air Force has requested 360 missiles, up from an initial target of 300. According to the president, Kyiv hopes to secure 5–10% of U.S. stocks, with Ukraine prepared to pay for the missiles.
Zelensky also said Germany had agreed to provide 600 PAC-2 missiles for Patriot systems in 2027–2028, while negotiations with Washington over additional supplies continue.
Longer-term alternatives to the Patriot are also moving ahead, the president said, referring specifically to the Freyja project, a joint effort by European and Ukrainian defense companies to produce a new anti-ballistic missile system.
The project has moved from political discussions to the technical stage, with companies now beginning practical work, Zelensky said.

articles.body:
Ukrainian forces strike Russian Iskander launcher near Ukraine’s border – Zelensky
President Volodymyr Zelensky said this while speaking with journalists, according to Ukrinform.
“Today we have another success. We cannot provide many details because of the sensitivity of the operation, but the fact remains. We struck an Iskander launcher near our border. I am grateful to our soldiers who carried this out. This is our operation to hunt down their systems deployed nearby,” he said.
According to the president, striking launchers is one of the ways to counter Russian strikes.
“In other words, this is one of the ways to fight back when our anti-ballistic missiles are limited. There is another tactic — it is more difficult, and we have developed it — hunting down their nearby sites from which ballistic missiles are launched. This is a separate effort, a separate program, a separate operation. And today we managed to carry it out. Our Defense Forces have simply done a great job,” Zelensky added.
Read also: Ukraine’s anti-ballistic missile defense to be like F-16s and millions of drones – Zelensky
As previously reported by Ukrinform, Ukraine and its European partners have agreed to jointly develop the Freya anti-ballistic missile defense system, which is intended to combine Ukrainian missile technologies with European radars, sensors, and control systems.
The project already involves Eurosam, the manufacturer of the SAMP/T system, as well as Leonardo, Thales, and Saab.
The project’s lead industrial partner is Ukrainian company Fire Point, which developed the Flamingo cruise missile. Last month, the company announced an agreement with the German defense manufacturer HENSOLDT to supply a radar for the system.

articles.title: Zelenskyy meets US senators: sanctions and ballistic missile defence discussed
articles.body:
Zelenskyy meets US senators: sanctions and ballistic missile defence discussed
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with US senators from both parties – Richard Blumenthal and James Lankford – in Kyiv on 23 August.
Source: Zelenskyy on X (Twitter), as reported by European Pravda
Details: Zelenskyy thanked the American lawmakers for their unwavering bipartisan and bicameral support, referring to the anti-Russia sanctions bill championed by the late Senator Lindsey Graham.
"We appreciate that work continues in both chambers of the US Congress to increase pressure on Russia, and we hope that Lindsey Graham's bill on sanctions against Russia and Iran can ultimately be passed," he stressed.
Zelenskyy briefed the senators on Russia's constant ballistic missile terror and emphasised that Ukraine must have the capabilities to counter such strikes. According to him, Washington granting licences for Patriot production "could significantly help".
They also discussed cooperation between Ukraine and the US, bilateral agreements and prospective projects.
Background:
- On 7 August, the US Senate approved the sanctions bill against Russia with 86 votes in favour. The bill was co-authored by the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham and Democrat Richard Blumenthal. It concerns "punitive" tariffs on countries that import Russian energy resources.
- Further consideration in the House of Representatives and passage are possible no earlier than September – lawmakers are on recess until 31 August.
- US President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his wish for the bill to include provisions on Iran but indicated he is prepared to sign it out of respect for the late Graham.

articles.title: Prime minister in Kyiv: Russia shouldn't count on us tiring of Ukraine support
articles.body:
Prime minister in Kyiv: Russia shouldn't count on us tiring of Ukraine support
Ukraine must receive everything it needs to defend itself, Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) said as he arrived in Kyiv for an NB8 summit with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Michal is in the Ukrainian capital on Sunday and will co-chair a summit of Nordic-Baltic (NB8) and Ukrainian leaders with Zelenskyy, and will take part in events marking Ukraine's National Flag Day.
Estonia holds the NB8 presidency this year, and Michal's visit comes at a time of intensified attacks by Russia on Kyiv and Ukraine and stalled diplomatic efforts.
The visit also closely follows the 35th anniversary of the restoration of Estonian independence. "This year marks 35 years since Estonia restored its independence and Ukraine declared its independence. Both our countries secured the right to decide their own future. Today, Ukraine is defending that right on the battlefield while standing up for the freedom and security of all Europe," Michal said.
The Nordic and Baltic countries have stood with Ukraine since the first day of Russia's full-scale war of aggression, now in its fifth year. "Ukraine must receive everything it needs to defend itself and resist Russian aggression," the prime minister went on, via a press release.
He noted that "everything Ukraine needs" primarily means more air defense, more ammunition and greater investment in Ukraine's defense industry. "At the same time, we must increase pressure on Russia, strengthen sanctions and close the loopholes Russia uses to evade them," Michal added.
"We are helping Ukraine prepare for winter and protect and restore critical energy infrastructure, which remains under threat because of Russia's brutality," the head of government went on.
While in Kyiv, Michal will meet his Ukrainian counterpart, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi, to discuss bilateral relations and preparations for the Ukraine Recovery Conference to be held in Tallinn in January next year.
Michal's visit also coincides with Ukraine's National Flag Day, which is marked annually on August 23.
The NB8 format brings together the Nordic countries — Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden — and the Baltic states — Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania — for regular dialogue on security and regional issues. Following the summit, a joint press conference is expected to outline outcomes and new commitments, as Estonia's NB8 presidency has placed regional security and support for Ukraine at the top of the agenda.
Estonia has been one of Ukraine's strongest supporters since the full-scale invasion began in February 2022, providing military aid, humanitarian assistance and political backing, while consistently calling for increased international pressure on Russia. The Reconstruction Conference in Tallinn next January will bring together international partners to coordinate Ukraine's long-term recovery, and Michal's visit continues a pattern of high-level engagement between the two countries.
Michal's visit is scheduled to last one day, with the prime minister returning to Estonia later Sunday.
The summit comes as diplomatic efforts to end the war remain stalled, with Russia insisting any deal must reflect "realities on the ground" — a reference to its control of around one-fifth of Ukrainian territory. On the battlefield, fighting has intensified, while Russia continues its long-range strikes on Ukrainian cities . Ukraine has expanded its own deep strikes inside Russia.

articles.title: Iran made billions of dollars, bypassed sanctions amid US blockade, top official Rezaee claims
articles.body:
Iran has made billions of dollars despite sanctions and amid the United States blockade, Supreme National Security Council head Mohsen Rezaee claimed in an interview with the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB) station on Saturday.
He also stated that Iran had sold millions of barrels of oil, bypassing the US naval blockade.
"In the past month or two, we sold seventy million barrels of oil," he said. "Now every day we sell oil to American ships on that side, as much as we produce."
He also warned that other countries should not join the US "economic war" against Iran, threatening to strike any that participated.
"Of course, we negotiate with him first," he said. "We hold a meeting, we say, 'go and separate your ranks from America,' and if they don't act, we will strike. We will strike the interests of the country."
In addition, Rezaee threatened the US, claiming that Iran had not attacked American bases unprovoked before. Now that the US had declared economic warfare, he explained, Iran would strike "a few oil and economic companies around Iran and elsewhere."
Iran would also attack bases if the US added forces to it, he said.
"They will not make any movements in the southern direction," he added. "We will find out if they have met with the counter-revolutionary groups. We will attack them there."
US, Israel aiming to promote war to sell more weapons, Iran claims
During the interview, Rezaee accused the US and Israel of intentionally fostering the regional conflicts in order to sell weaponry, saying that Iran had no interest in the war.
"If we were warmongers, would we have gone to three negotiations with the Americans?" he defended. "How many ceasefires would we have accepted? Of course, we are not warmongers, but we will not surrender under any circumstances. We will defend our nation wholeheartedly."
The Strait of Hormuz is currently closed, he also claimed, and will reopen only if the US "fulfills its obligations."
Discussing the Mecca defense pact between Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia, Rezaee claimed that the Gulf countries had been spurred by the US abandoning them.
"America told them, 'Goodbye, we are leaving.' They want to fill America's void."
Iran would also be evolving its defenses in the wake of the war with Israel and the US, he said, saying that "Iran today will no longer be the Iran it was before the war.
"Of course, the pretentious and arrogant America will not be the America it was before the war," he added.
US President Donald Trump's "stupidity," he said, came in creating a huge debt for Americans and their allies.
"He wanted to make America great again with his election slogan, but what did he make great?" he said. "He made the debts greater. The debt on the 30-year US bond rate has become greater."
In order to finance itself now, Razaee claimed, the US "must borrow at a rate of three and seven tenths of 2020, meaning that for every hundred billion dollars in debt, it must spend three and seven tenths of a billion dollars more annually than in the past. If you multiply this by the thirty-year US bonds in those 40 trillion bonds, perhaps several times our annual budget is imposed on the American people and American companies."
US endangered world by attacking Iran over nuclear weapon, Razaee accuses
The Supreme National Security Council head also addressed the US claims that it had begun the war with Iran in order to prevent it from acquiring nuclear weapons, accusing America that by doing so it had actually put the world in greater danger.
"The United States said it came to prevent the atomic bomb," he explained. "Now the whole world is saying, 'Wow, neither the NPT [Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons] nor membership in the Atomic Energy Organization is effective. And it turned out that this atomic issue is very important. The United States has started a war. Why shouldn't we go after the atomic bomb?'"
Iran, Razaee claimed, had accepted the presence of IAEA inspectors, numerous checks and forms of supervision, and other concessions for its nuclear energy projects.
"Well, now the world says that if Iran, which has been so obedient, is attacked, and its nuclear facilities are attacked, why don't we go and make a bomb so that no one can attack us?"

articles.title: Russia’s New Banderol Missile Ends Up in Belarus After Veering Away From Ukraine
articles.body:

Russia’s New Banderol Missile Ends Up in Belarus After Veering Away From Ukraine
Several Russian S8000 Banderol cruise missiles crossed into Belarus during Moscow’s massive attack on Ukraine, with at least one reportedly flying around 75 miles into Belarusian territory before running out of fuel and crashing into a field, according to OSINT community Oko Gora on August 22.
Ukrainian monitoring channels tracked multiple Banderol weapons entering Belarus beginning at around 4 am, while a Belarusian military aircraft was scrambled from Baranovichi airfield.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Separate reports indicated that a Su-30 fighter was sent up as one of the weapons moved deeper into the country.
According to Ukrainian monitoring resource Monitor, one Banderol traveled approximately 120 kilometers, or 75 miles, inside Belarus without being brought down by Belarusian Su-30s. It eventually exhausted its fuel supply and fell into a field. The circumstances could not be independently verified.
Other monitoring reports indicated that at least 12 Russian Banderol missile-drones entered Belarusian airspace during the attack. It remains unclear whether any were destroyed or disrupted using electronic warfare.
The incursion came during another large-scale Russian aerial attack on Ukraine.
Ukraine’s Air Force said its defenses destroyed or suppressed 191 aerial targets between the evening of August 21 and the morning of August 22, including three Kh-31P/Kh-59 missiles, six Banderol munitions and 182 drones. Russian strikes were recorded at 41 locations, while debris from intercepted weapons fell at another 12 sites.
Russia also launched 217 attack drones, including Shahed-type UAVs, Gerbera drones and decoys. More than 50 were jet-powered, according to the Ukrainian Air Force.
The S8000 Banderol is a relatively new Russian weapon combining characteristics of a cruise missile and long-range attack drone. Developed by Russia’s Kronstadt company, it has an estimated range of roughly 500 kilometers, or 310 miles.
Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence says Russia can produce up to 80 Banderol missiles per month. The weapon reportedly cruises at 520-560 kilometers per hour and can reach maximum speeds of 620-650 kilometers per hour.
Earlier, a Russian “Banderol” missile crossed from the Odesa region into Moldova on August 17, Ukraine’s Air Force reported, before an unidentified aircraft crashed near the village of Tălmaza in the country’s Ștefan Vodă district.

articles.title: Putin wants to draft 300,000 new troops, Zelensky says
articles.body:
Putin wants to draft 300,000 new troops, Zelensky says
- Ukraine says Russia plans to draft 300,000 new troops after September elections to boost its war effort, aiming for 500,000 overall by 2027, focusing on peripheral regions.
- Russia is increasing missile production to 1,300 per year and escalating air attacks on Ukrainian cities, while Ukraine faces a shortage of missile interceptors.
- Ukraine expects a tough winter with more Russian strikes on energy, has defence funding gaps, and secured new air-defence system deals with France and Germany.
AI generated
KYIV - Ukraine thinks Russia is planning to draft an additional 300,000 troops for its war effort after Russian parliamentary elections in mid-September, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said.
Moscow’s forces are pressing ahead with an effort to capture the rest of eastern Ukraine’s industrialised Donbas region, where its troops have ground forward at what Kyiv says is a great cost.
In comments to reporters released on Aug 23, Zelensky said Russia could draft more troops in 2027 to reach an overall goal of 500,000, part of what he described as a “peripheral mobilisation” targeting Russia’s far-flung regions.
“We believe it will not take place in the central cities,” he said. “But I don’t think they will be able to hide it very well.”
Parliamentary elections in Russia are set for Sept 18 to 20.
As fighting rages around the strategic city of Kostiantynivka, Zelensky said Russia was losing a “maximum” amount of troops in its bid to advance into Ukraine’s so-called fortress belt of eastern cities.
He also hailed recent gains by Kyiv’s troops in southeastern Ukraine, adding that the amount of territory occupied by Russia and liberated by Ukrainian forces in 2026 would be equal.
Russia ramping up missile output, Zelensky says
Russia is bolstering its battlefield offensive with an escalating air war on Ukrainian cities made worse by a critical shortage of US-designed Patriot interceptors.
Zelensky said the 264 interceptors Ukraine is expecting to have received in 2026 represent a significant drop from 2025, when Ukraine received 364, and 2023, when it received 675.
He added that Russia was aiming to develop a capacity to produce up to 1,300 ballistic missiles per year.
Over the summer, Ukraine has escalated a campaign of drone strikes targeting Russian economic infrastructure, including oil refineries and online retailers’ warehouses, seeking to destroy infrastructure it says is central to Russia’s war effort.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said in comments on Aug 22 that Kyiv had opened “Pandora’s box” by striking economic targets, saying Russia would hit back at Ukraine’s “most sensitive economic sectors”.
Ukraine braces for new energy strikes, faces funding gap
Zelensky said Ukraine was facing another difficult winter of Russian strikes on its energy grid, a prospect that had prompted Kyiv’s air force to ask for 360 missile interceptors for the season.
He also said he had reached an agreement with France on at least one SAMP/T air-defence system this year, and with Germany on the supply of about 600 PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors through 2028.
Ukraine’s war effort is further complicated by a US$27 billion (S$34.3 billion) defence funding gap in 2026, Zelensky said, a result of higher-than-expected spending in the first half of the year.
At least US$8 billion is needed for “a normal start” to 2027, plus about US$20 billion more for military salaries, payments to families of the dead, as well as other financing, he added. REUTERS

articles.title: Economic warfare: Bankrupting Iran will be more effective than bombing - opinion
articles.body:
The US and Israel have demonstrated what military power can do to Iran. Bombs can destroy missile factories, military installations, drone warehouses, and command centers.
But there is another weapon that may ultimately prove even more decisive than another bombing campaign.
The Iranian regime can rebuild a destroyed factory if it has the money to do so. It can replace missiles, drones, and military equipment if it has access to foreign currency, international markets, and the financial networks necessary to acquire the materials it needs.
That is why the next phase of this war should not be measured only by how many bombs America drops on Iran. It should also be measured by how effectively the United States can cut Tehran off from the money it needs to rebuild its military, fund terrorism, and maintain its grip on power.
Iran is already breaking
The numbers coming out of Iran are staggering. The war has caused approximately $270 billion in damage, equivalent to roughly 57% of Iran's GDP. The scale of that destruction suggests that Iran's recovery will take years, perhaps decades.
Even more alarming for Tehran is the compounding effect of the war. Each additional month of conflict could set the Iranian economy back by more than five years because of the destruction of capital stock, infrastructure, and productivity.
History shows how quickly economic damage can spread once the foundations of an economy begin to weaken. As businesses lose capital, productivity declines, investment disappears, and confidence collapses, the damage can move far beyond the original crisis and become increasingly difficult to reverse.
Iran entered this war economically weakened by decades of sanctions, corruption, mismanagement, inflation, currency collapse, and international isolation. Now the regime faces the enormous cost of rebuilding while its economy continues to deteriorate.
Meanwhile, ordinary Iranians are already suffering under rising prices, declining purchasing power, and a weakening currency. This is not simply an economic statistic. It is the daily reality of families struggling to afford basic necessities.
But we must make an important distinction. The Persian people are not our enemy. The mullahs are. The tragedy is that Iran is a nation with extraordinary natural resources, an educated population, and one of the world's great civilizations. Yet the Islamic Republic has squandered its wealth on missiles, terrorism, and foreign wars while millions of Iranians struggle at home.
Trump's 'Economic D-Day'
With peace negotiations deadlocked and the war continuing, President Trump has now escalated the economic pressure under the banner of Operation Economic Fury.
Trump called it an “Economic D-Day” and warned that the United States would impose severe secondary sanctions against any nation's financial institutions, businesses, airports, or governments that facilitate Iranian trade.
The message is unmistakable: nations and institutions will have to choose. They can do business with the United States, or they can help keep the Iranian regime alive.
For years, Tehran has survived sanctions by constructing an underground financial network comprising front companies, shadow banking systems, exchange houses, oil-smuggling operations, and intermediaries. These networks allow the regime to move money and sell its products despite international restrictions.
America must systematically dismantle them. If a bank knowingly helps Tehran move money, it should face consequences. If a company launders Iranian oil revenue, it should lose access to the American financial system. If a shipping network disguises Iranian petroleum, it should be exposed and sanctioned.
Access to the American financial system is not a right. No institution should be allowed to finance the world's leading state sponsor of terrorism while continuing to benefit from the American economy.
Destroy the ability to rebuild
This is the strategic difference between bombing Iran and bankrupting the regime. Bombs destroy what Iran has today. Economic warfare can destroy Iran's ability to rebuild tomorrow. That should be America's objective.
The Iranian regime needs money to pay the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, manufacture missiles and drones, maintain its military infrastructure, and finance Hezbollah, Hamas, the Houthis, and other terrorist proxies.
Follow the money, and you find the regime's power. Cut off that money, and the Islamic Republic faces a far greater threat than the destruction of another military installation. A regime can survive a destroyed building, but it faces a much more serious problem when it cannot pay its security forces, finance its proxies, replace its weapons, or maintain the patronage networks that keep it in power.
Do not give Tehran a financial lifeline
This is where Washington must not blink. There will always be pressure to release frozen Iranian assets, ease sanctions, restore trade, and provide Tehran with billions of dollars in exchange for promises. America has seen that movie before and should not repeat the mistake of giving Tehran economic relief in exchange for vague assurances that cannot be trusted.
The Iranian regime should not receive another dollar in economic relief without concrete, verifiable, and irreversible concessions. There can be no return to business as usual while Tehran retains the ability to rebuild its military machine and finance terrorist organizations throughout the Middle East.
Any relief must follow genuine compliance, not empty promises. Iran must demonstrate that it is prepared to abandon the policies that have destabilized the region for decades. Otherwise, America risks financing the very regime it is trying to defeat.
Bankrupt the regime, not the people
The Persian people deserve better. They deserve an Iran where national wealth is invested in families, education, businesses, infrastructure, and opportunity rather than missiles, militias, and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
America has already demonstrated that it can inflict devastating military damage on Iran. The next challenge is to ensure that the regime does not have the financial resources to restore the military and terrorist infrastructure it has lost. That means closing financial loopholes and dismantling the international networks that allow Tehran to sell oil, move money, and evade sanctions.
President Trump has now put economic warfare at the center of the conflict through Operation Economic Fury. If America follows through with precision and determination, this strategy could prove more consequential than another round of bombing.
Cut off the money that funds terrorism, and the regime loses its ability to project terror. Break the financial backbone of the Islamic Republic, and the Persian people may finally have an opportunity to break free from the regime that has oppressed them for nearly half a century.
The objective is not to destroy Iran. It is to bankrupt the regime that has stolen Iran's future, financed terror across the Middle East, and kept its own people in chains.
The war may not ultimately be decided by the last missile fired.
It may be decided by the last dollar Tehran can spend.

Zelenskyy: Russia could produce up to 1,300 ballistic missiles a year, currently has around 600
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that Russia has the potential to produce up to 1,300 ballistic missiles a year, and currently has around 600-630 such missiles at its disposal.
Source: Zelenskyy speaking to journalists, as reported by Ukrinform
Details: According to Zelenskyy, Russia is aiming to reach a production rate of around 100 ballistic missiles a month, but has not yet achieved that level.
Quote: "I believe Russia could produce up to 1,300 ballistic missiles a year. Now they have 600-630. We have a fairly good understanding of the volume they're aiming for between now and the end of winter.
They could potentially reach around 100 ballistic missiles a month. But they don't have that yet."
Details: Zelenskyy said that the defence forces are working to reduce the capabilities of Russia's military industry, including striking military facilities linked to missile production.
He noted that Ukrainian air defence has become more effective at shooting down Russian cruise missiles thanks to combat aviation, IRIS-T and Hawk air defence systems, though countering ballistic missiles remains more difficult.
The president also said that Ukraine is carrying out specific operations aimed at disrupting preparations for massive Russian missile attacks.
Quote: "I think you've seen recently that at some point they were planning a strike but didn't carry it out.
That's not a coincidence. We're working to prevent them from being able to carry out massive missile attacks."
Details: Zelenskyy added that Ukraine's Armed Forces had struck a Russian Iskander missile system near the Ukrainian border. He did not give an exact date or location.

articles.title: Ukraine’s ousted defense minister confirms M&M’s operation planning and discloses real story behind its name
articles.body:
Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has confirmed that Kyiv had planned an operation against targets in Moscow. Recently, The Atlantic reported that at the beginning of 2026, Kyiv had planned Operation M&M’s, which involved using AI-powered drones against Moscow's airports to paralyze them.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned at the time that if any of the drones struck a civilian aircraft, Ukraine’s actions could be perceived as an act of piracy. Nevertheless, work on implementing the plan began.
Sources in the Office of the President have declined to confirm the organization of the operation in comments to journalists. However, former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who initiated the operation and whose departure from office led to the plan being shelved, did confirm it.
Why M&M’s?
In an interview with 24 Channel, Fedorov declined to explain the idea behind the operation, adding that it could still be implemented in the future.
But he provided details on the operation’s codename, saying journalists had misinterpreted it, as the plan had nothing to do with deploying a large number of cheap drones.
“That is a mistake. At a meeting where we were discussing fully autonomous deep-strike drones, I was handing out M&M’s to everyone. It was my birthday, and someone gave me a box of M&M’s. I shared them with everyone and said that we would call this autonomous-drone project M&M’s," Fedorov said.
What does the former minister plan to do next?
During the interview, Fedorov said he wants to create a venture fund to attract Western capital for investment in Ukrainian startups and developers.
“I have several priorities. One is cheap missiles, because I am convinced that they are the future of warfare involving artificial intelligence. These are inexpensive missiles that could be used to deter strikes and further escalation," he explained.
Another priority for him is the robotization of the front line and the deployment of sensors.
"We need to think about how to remove infantry from the front line. We need to robotize the front line as much as possible so that people do not have to spend months in dugouts under drone attacks," he said.
Opposition to the system
Fedorov also announced that he planned to travel to the US the following week, not to seek President Donald Trump’s support after calls for Ukraine to hold elections.
When asked whether he planned to meet Elon Musk there and continue their cooperation in some form, the former minister replied, “We’ll see.”
He said he did not yet know whether he would run for president or parliament, or, if so, which political team he would join, adding that everything would become clear only after it was possible to prepare for a vote.
The former minister also said that he was currently in opposition—not to any particular politician, but to the system.
“We are not talking about one person, or two people, or just some top officials. We are talking about hundreds of people who have simply become accustomed over the years to making money from the state budget,” he said.

Source: Zelenskyy speaking to journalists on 23 August, as cited by Interfax-Ukraine and reported by European Pravda
Details: According to Zelenskyy, Ukraine needs 300-360 missiles for Patriot air defence systems, while a total of 600 such missiles are produced per year.
Quote: "I wanted to find 300 Patriot missiles for the winter package. The request from our Air Force is 360. But when only 600 are produced a year, 360 is not easy to come by. We're working with countries on additional options. And I'd really like to believe we can find a way to get some small percentage of US stocks – say, 5% or 10%. And we're ready to pay for that supply. That way, America could replenish its stockpile, and we could get through the winter. Such a political decision by America regarding the supply of missiles could change a great deal, both in terms of protecting lives and diplomatically."
Details: Meanwhile, Zelenskyy said he had agreed with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on the supply of 600 PAC-2 missiles for 2027-2028.
"PAC-2 can also shoot down ballistic missiles, you just need more of them," the president noted.
Zelenskyy also spoke about talks with the American side.
Quote: "The Americans are seriously increasing production in the second half of 2027 and beyond. But that takes time, unfortunately. So we keep talking to them now about the volumes we need – the volumes are actually there."
Details: The president said Ukraine received 675 missiles throughout the whole of 2023, while in 2025 it received 364, even though Russian missile strikes have increased over that period. In 2026, deliveries of 264 PAC-3 and PAC-2 missiles are planned.
Quote: "PAC-3 is what we receive from the US through the PURL programme. All our partners – both the Americans and the Europeans – understand exactly how much money they're transferring and exactly how many missiles they're giving us. There are also some separate bilateral agreements with individual European countries and Middle Eastern countries. But you can see there's unfortunately a downward trend, and that depends primarily on the American side."
Background:
- The same day, Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine will receive new radars for its air defence systems, following a call with French President Emmanuel Macron.
- According to the Financial Times, US President Donald Trump turned down Zelenskyy's request for hundreds of additional Patriot interceptor missiles, citing America's own needs in the Middle East.
- Trump has also backtracked after earlier positive signals that he might grant Ukraine a licence to produce Patriot missiles, saying he has not yet made a final decision.

Denmark to continue providing military aid to Ukraine, PM says

In an interview with Russian state media propagandist Pavel Zarubin, Putin claimed that Russian strikes on Ukraine impact the course of combat operations in the “most direct and positive way.”

Addressing the recent Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries and infrastructure, Putin attempted to reassure the Russian public, claiming that Ukraine had failed to achieve a turning point in the conflict.
He asserted that Russian forces have increased the pace of their offensive and are “confidently solving the tasks” of what Moscow calls its “special military operation.”
The Russian leader stated that by targeting Russian economic sites, Kyiv had “opened a Pandora’s box.” Putin claimed that Russia’s retaliatory strikes are “more destructive” than the Ukrainian attacks on Russian territory, despite Russia’s systematic targeting of Ukrainian civilian infrastructure since the beginning of the full-scale invasion.
During the interview, Putin also dismissed Ukrainian proposals for a ceasefire as “exotic and unacceptable,” accusing Kyiv of attempting to intimidate Russians and disrupt the country’s simulated elections.
Fires Ravage Logistics Sites in Russia’s Orenburg and St. Petersburg
Deadly double-tap strike on Kryvyi Rih mall
Putin’s comments defending Russian strikes coincided with rescue operations in Kryvyi Rih, where authorities reported that nine people, including two children, remained missing after a Russian double-tap drone attack on a major shopping center.
The afternoon attack struck the mall in two waves. According to Ukrainian officials, the second drone hit approximately 30 minutes after the first, specifically targeting the emergency responders who had arrived to extinguish fires and search for survivors.
The strike killed 16 people and injured 140, including 23 children. At least 29 of the injured were reported in serious condition.
President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the attack on his hometown as deliberate.
“An absolutely cynical and despicable strike was carried out by the Russians against an ordinary shopping center in Kryvyi Rih,” Zelensky said. “Attacks like these are nothing less than terrorist acts. And the world must respond to them accordingly – with real pressure on the aggressor.”

articles.title: North Carolina firm to supply parts for Marine Corps’ NMESIS launcher
articles.body:
- Corvid Technologies received a $33.86 million sole-source IDIQ contract to build a weapon sled assembly for the NMESIS anti-ship missile launcher.
- The Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps issued the award under FAR 6.302-1, with no funds obligated until individual task orders are placed through August 2034.
Corvid Technologies LLC has been awarded a $33.86 million contract to build a weapon sled assembly for the Navy/Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction System, the U.S. Marine Corps’ land-based anti-ship missile launcher.
The award is an indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract combining firm-fixed-price, cost-plus-fixed-fee, and cost reimbursement terms. Work will be performed at Corvid’s facilities in Mooresville, North Carolina, where the company is headquartered. The contract’s ordering period runs through August 2034, giving the Department of War nearly nine years to place orders against it.
No funds were obligated at the time of award, meaning the Department of War has not yet committed any money against the $33.86 million ceiling. The Department of War will issue individual task orders and delivery orders as the work is scheduled, and money will be committed against those orders rather than the base contract.
The Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps, based at Quantico, Virginia, is the contracting activity, and the award carries the contract number M67854-26-D-1008.
The contract was not competitively bid, meaning the Department of War did not solicit offers from other companies before making the award. It was issued under Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1, which allows agencies to sole-source a requirement when only one company can reasonably meet it.
NMESIS pairs the Naval Strike Missile with the ROGUE Fires carrier, an unmanned launch vehicle that Oshkosh Defense builds on the Joint Light Tactical Vehicle chassis. Raytheon, an RTX business, produces the Naval Strike Missile in partnership with Norway’s Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace. The missile has a stated range of roughly 185 km (115 miles). It is designed to fly low over the sea to avoid radar detection before striking a ship near the waterline.
A weapon sled assembly is a structural component of a missile launcher. It supports and positions a missile canister on the launch platform before firing. The Department of War announcement does not specify further design details, integration requirements, or which portion of the NMESIS system the assembly will serve.
NMESIS entered low-rate initial production in 2024, after the Department of War awarded Raytheon a contract worth nearly $50 million to begin building launcher units, with deliveries due by August 2027. The U.S. Marine Corps fielded its first six NMESIS systems to the 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment at Marine Corps Base Hawaii in November 2024. Marine Corps Systems Command has said the service ultimately plans to field 48 NMESIS launchers.
Marines took NMESIS to the Philippines for Exercise Balikatan in April and May 2025, staging a launcher on Batan Island in the Luzon Strait. In June 2026, the 12th Marine Littoral Regiment on Okinawa, Japan, received its own NMESIS launchers, giving the unit land-based anti-ship missiles along the first island chain.
NMESIS is organized under Medium-Range Missile batteries within Marine Littoral Regiments, formations built for Expeditionary Advanced Base Operations. Naval News reported, citing a Marine Corps release, that each battery is structured into six sections of three launchers, for a total of 18 anti-ship missile systems per battery. A separate system, the Marine Air Defense Integrated System, provides close-in protection for NMESIS batteries against drones and aircraft.
Corvid Technologies is a small, employee-owned defense contractor founded in 2004 and based in Mooresville. The company employs more than 200 engineers and scientists. It specializes in computational physics modeling and uses an in-house supercomputer to simulate high-rate physical events such as blast and ballistic impacts. Corvid holds an 8(a) small business designation and has previously worked with the Missile Defense Agency and the U.S. Navy.
The company’s existing Navy work includes a contract for short and medium range sub-orbital target vehicles used in missile defense testing, awarded in 2025 and valued at up to $268.4 million, and a potential 10-year, $385 million contract to support Missile Defense Agency test instrumentation. Corvid has also served as a subcontractor to Kratos Defense on Department of War hypersonic flight test work.

articles.title: One Russian warehouse smolders near Kazakhstan while a bigger fire rages near St. Petersburg
articles.body:
Ukrainian drones struck a logistics complex belonging to Russian online retailer Ozon in Orenburg on 23 August, the second Ozon warehouse hit in two days, monitoring Telegram channels reported. The site sits about 1,200 km from the war zone, near Russia's border with Kazakhstan. Hours earlier, a large fire tore through a separate warehouse outside St. Petersburg, roughly 900 km north of Ukraine, though local authorities declared no drone or missile threat.
Drones hit Russia's biggest Ozon warehouse
Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ published video of the strike moment, after which a fire took hold on the site. Independent Russian outlet Astra analyzed eyewitness footage showing an emergency vehicle racing toward the depot. The complex spans more than 200,000 m² and was designed to hold over 31 million items, ranking among Ozon's biggest in Russia.
The warehouse stands inside the city's special economic zone, a tax-favored industrial park on the eastern edge of European Russia. The first phase opened in August 2024, and a second building followed in 2025.
Orenburg mayor Albert Yumadilov claimed several drones were downed over the special economic zone and that debris fell on the Ozon complex, starting a fire that crews quickly put out with no one hurt.
Ozon confirmed the strike, saying it evacuated more than 300 workers, pulled its goods from the marketplace and stopped taking new deliveries while the site sat idle.
A second fire near St. Petersburg, with no air-raid alert
Overnight, a large blaze hit a warehouse in the Kolpino area south of St. Petersburg. Astra established that the warehouse stood about 350 m from an Ozon site, and witnesses said they heard no drones or air defense. Ukrainian Telegram channel Exile+ identified the burning facility as a storage warehouse run by Logistera.
Part of a widening campaign on Russian marketplace logistics
The Orenburg hit followed the first-ever Ozon strike a day earlier, at a warehouse in Chapaevsk, Samara Oblast. Before turning to Ozon, Ukrainian drones had struck more than 10 warehouses belonging to the larger Russian marketplace Wildberries. Such marketplace hubs move not only consumer goods but dual-use items like electronics and drone components that can reach Russia's military.

articles.title: Ukraine moves to practical work on ballistic missile defense - Zelenskyy spoke about two key projects
articles.body:
Ukraine moves to practical work on ballistic missile defense - Zelenskyy spoke about two key projects
Kyiv • UNN
Ukraine is moving from political agreements to practical work on ballistic missile defense. Kyiv is simultaneously developing the pan-European Freyja shield project and producing its own analogues of the missile used by Patriot systems.
Ukraine is moving from political agreements to practical work on its own anti-ballistic capabilities, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. Work is underway in two directions at once - the pan-European Freyja anti-ballistic shield and the production of a Ukrainian analogue of missiles for Patriot, reports UNN.
Details
Our anti-ballistic capabilities have several directions. The European direction is our joint Freyja project with Europe, and we are counting heavily on this program. The other direction is Raytheon. We are talking about the possibility of building a Ukrainian missile for the Patriot system. They view this idea positively. They selected a company that can do this - Fire Point. I met with Raytheon in the United States, and we agreed to move forward with this project. After that, they held their first technical meeting with the Ukrainian side regarding the details. Now we will wait for their response. I think we will receive it in the coming weeks. We will get an answer regarding the timeline and an understanding of whether it will succeed or not
In addition, the Freyja project is already moving from political agreements to practical work. European companies are beginning to join the technical implementation of the program directly.
The project has now moved from the leaders' positive reaction and willingness to work to the technical level. Companies are beginning to work in this direction in earnest
Earlier, Fire Point CEO Iryna Terekh told UNN that Freyja is at the stage of integrating key components into a single system—radars, a launcher, a command center, and the interceptor missile itself. Testing of individual system components is ongoing.
Russia plans to produce 1,300 ballistic missiles per year
Creating two options at once for Ukraine's anti-ballistic protection, which can be integrated into the European security system, is critically important. After all, as Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, Moscow seeks to reach a ballistic missile production rate of "100 per month," or approximately 1,300 per year. Ukraine has information that Russia currently has accumulated 600–630 ballistic missiles.
Russia could have up to 1,300 ballistic missiles per year. They currently have 600–630. We have an approximate understanding of the level they expect to reach from today through the end of winter. They could have approximately 100 ballistic missiles per month. They do not have that capability yet. We are working to weaken their military industry; there are relevant tasks involving strikes on military targets and other anti-ballistic sanctions
Thus, the third track of anti-ballistic protection for Ukraine is finding 300 missiles for the Patriot system. Obviously, Russia plans to use all those accumulated missiles to strike civilian populations and Ukrainian businesses.
I wanted to find 300 Patriot missiles for the winter package. The request from our Air Force is 360. But when 600 are produced per year, 360 is not easy. We are working with countries on additional possibilities. And I would very much like to believe that we will be able to find a way to obtain some small percentage of the U.S. stockpiles, say 5% or 10%. We are ready to pay for these supplies. In other words, America could replenish its stockpile, and we could get through the winter
We remind you
Fire Point is simultaneously expanding its own production base for missile programs. As the company's CEO Iryna Terekh previously said, at the end of 2027 the company plans to launch a solid rocket fuel plant in Denmark with a total area of more than 120,000 square meters.
The facility will be built in several stages. It is intended to supply fuel for FP-7 missiles, FP-7.x interceptors, and boosters for Flamingo. According to Terekh, locating part of the production capabilities in Denmark makes it possible to create a predictable base protected from Russian strikes for scaling up production.
According to Fire Point's estimate, once it reaches its planned capacity, the plant will be able to produce solid propellant each year for more than 4,100 FP-7 ballistic missiles or FP-7.x ballistic interceptors. During martial law, the company's products are primarily planned to be directed toward Ukraine's needs, while subsequently its production capabilities may also serve the European security system.

articles.title: 14 military targets and a second Ozon facility in two days: Ukraine intensifies strikes on Russia
articles.body:
14 military targets and a second Ozon facility in two days: Ukraine intensifies strikes on Russia
Kyiv • UNN
Ukrainian forces struck 14 Russian military targets, including a Su-33, a MiG-29, an Orion UAV, radars, and an S-400 system. At the same time, the Armed Forces of Ukraine attacked an Ozon logistics hub in Orenburg — the company's second facility in two days.
Ukraine continues to systematically take out Russian aircraft, air defenses, and rear logistics. On August 23, Commander of the Unmanned Systems Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Robert "Madyar" Brovdi published a list of 14 successfully hit military targets, while in Orenburg the Ozon logistics hub came under attack for the second time in two days. Fire Point-produced weapons were used in both operations, UNN reports.
Details
The main part of Madyar's list consists of elements of Russia's air defense. It includes eight radar stations, two surface-to-air missile systems, and an S-400 "Triumf" position.
Thus, of the 14 targets named by Madyar, three were Russian aircraft, while another 11 were part of the enemy's detection and air defense system.
Ozon came under attack for the second time in two days
At the same time, on the morning of August 23, an FP-1 strike drone manufactured by Fire Point hit the logistics complex of the Russian marketplace Ozon in Orenburg. The use of an FP-1 was confirmed to UNN by Fire Point co-owner and chief designer Denys Shtilerman.
For Ozon, this is already the second attack in two days.
On August 22, Ukrainian FP-1 drones hit the company's logistics hub in Chapayevsk, Samara region. The Chapayevsk hub was one of Ozon's largest logistics centers in the Volga region. After all phases were launched, its area amounted to approximately 135,000 square meters, its capacity exceeded 40 million items, and the complex could process more than 215,000 orders per day.
The Ministry of Defense of Ukraine explained the rationale behind the strikes on Russian logistics centers. The ministry emphasized that such facilities are used to store dual-use goods, and that systematically striking them complicates the enemy's logistics and hits the Russian economy.
After the strike on the hub in Chapayevsk, the Ministry of Defense stated that Ukrainian units had previously struck 15 of Wildberries' largest logistics hubs, and that now "it was Ozon's turn."
In fact, these are no longer isolated strikes on individual facilities. Ukraine is simultaneously taking out Russian air defense systems, aircraft, and infrastructure that ensures the movement of goods and supplies within the russian federation.

articles.title: Is Russia preparing an offensive against the Kyiv region: Zelenskyy named the conditions and a possible direction
articles.body:
Is Russia preparing an offensive against the Kyiv region: Zelenskyy named the conditions and a possible direction
Kyiv • UNN
Russia may try to advance into the Chernihiv and Kyiv regions to create a buffer zone. At present, there is no strike force near the border.
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated on August 23 that, in the future, Russia may attempt to launch an offensive from Bryansk Oblast in the Chernihiv–Kyiv direction, in particular to create a so-called "buffer zone." At the same time, there is currently no troop grouping near Ukraine's northern border necessary for such an operation, reports UNN.
Details
According to Zelenskyy, the Kremlin's further plans may depend on the situation in eastern Ukraine and the launch of a new wave of mobilization in the Russian Federation.
If he has the success there that he is counting on, then he may redistribute forces to another direction. For example, to create a "buffer zone." There could also be an operation in the Chernihiv–Kyiv regions
Zelenskyy noted that this concerns a possible offensive from Russian territory, specifically Bryansk Oblast. At the same time, Ukraine currently does not see the number of personnel necessary there to conduct a large-scale offensive operation, although it is detecting Russian military equipment near the border.
The president also stated that after the elections to the State Duma of the Russian Federation, the Russian authorities may carry out an additional mobilization of around 300,000 people. In the view of the Ukrainian leadership, most of this manpower could primarily be sent to eastern Ukraine, where Russia seeks to intensify its offensive actions.
Context
Ukrainian authorities have been reporting for several months on Russia's possible plans to intensify combat operations in northern Ukraine.
In May, Zelenskyy chaired a meeting of the Staff of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief dedicated to possible scenarios of Russian offensive operations in the Chernihiv–Kyiv direction. At the time, the president said that Ukrainian intelligence was analyzing several options for the enemy's actions, including from the territory of Bryansk Oblast and Belarus.
At the end of June, the then Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, Oleksandr Syrskyi, stated that the most likely scenario could be a Russian offensive from Bryansk Oblast specifically toward Chernihiv Oblast, rather than directly toward Kyiv. According to him, one of Russia's objectives could be to seize part of the border territory and force Ukraine to redeploy reserves there from other sections of the front.
At the same time, in August, Ukrainian intelligence and the State Border Guard Service reported that they had not detected the formation of a Russian strike force near the northern border.
Vadym Skibitskyi, Deputy Chief of the Main Intelligence Directorate of the Ministry of Defense, noted that, to create such a force, Russia would first need to carry out an additional mobilization. According to an assessment by Ukrainian intelligence, if it is conducted in the autumn of 2026, preparing a sufficient number of troops for a large-scale operation could take several months.
The State Border Guard Service also emphasized that it is not currently observing a buildup of Russian forces either near the border with Bryansk Oblast or on the territory of Belarus. At the same time, Ukraine continues to strengthen the defenses of its northern regions, fortifications, and border protection system.
Reminder
At the beginning of August, State Border Guard Service spokesperson Andrii Demchenko reported that the enemy was planning an invasion in Chernihiv Oblast in order to divert the Armed Forces of Ukraine.

articles.title: NCSIST releases information on Strong Bow missile
articles.body:
TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The National Chung Shan Institute of Science and Technology has released information about its new Strong Bow missile on its website.
The Strong Bow is a land-based, mid-tier system designed to counter tactical ballistic missiles, according to the institute. It can intercept incoming tactical ballistic missiles at medium altitude and form a layered interception network with lower-tier missile defense systems, it added.
The missile uses thrust-vector control during its terminal phase, maintaining excellent maneuverability even in the thin atmosphere, the institute said.
It is equipped with precision guidance and a directional warhead, along with an integrated composite rocket motor that improves manufacturability. Its active electronically scanned array radar supports target classification and identification, engagement of multiple tactical ballistic missile targets, electronic counter-countermeasures, and high-precision tracking.
Each mobile launcher contains four missile canisters.
The military plans to build at least 128 Strong Bow missiles. The system will be deployed alongside Sky Bow III and Patriot Advanced Capability-3 interceptors as part of the layered T-Dome air defense network.

articles.title: Russia Uses Air Shadow Fleet to Supply Forces in Africa
articles.body:
Russia is using a network of military and private aircraft, similar to its maritime “shadow fleet”, to sustain its forces in Africa’s Sahel.
At least 75 flights linked to Russian state-aligned military forces travelled to Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger between January 2025 and July 2026, according to an analysis by the Center for Advanced Defense Studies (C4ADS).
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
The network resembles the logic of Russia’s better-known maritime “shadow fleet” of tankers used to export sanctioned Russian oil: rather than relying exclusively on clearly identifiable state assets, Moscow uses a mix of military operators, government agencies and private carriers to keep its supply lines running.
The most active operator was Flight Unit 224, a Russian defence ministry-controlled carrier already under US sanctions, the study found. But the study also identified Sapsan Airlines, Liz Aviation and Russia’s ‘Ministry for Emergency Situations’ among operators not sanctioned by the EU, US or UK.
The flights point to a broader logistics system rather than isolated movements. State aircraft regularly travelled through Russian-controlled bases in Syria and Libya, while private carriers tended to use commercial hubs in Turkey, Algeria and the UAE.
Tomáš Zdechovský, Czech EPP MEP and First Lieutenant in the Czech Army said the findings should trigger an urgent assessment by the EU institutions and member states.
Ukraine Destroys Su-24M at Saky, Hits Primorsko-Akhtarsk Airfield
“If these aircraft and companies are knowingly transporting Russian military personnel or military-related cargo to support the Africa Corps, they should face targeted sanctions, regardless of where the aircraft are registered,” he told Euractiv.
Brussels has progressively expanded its targeting of Russia’s maritime shadow fleet, including companies and other enablers based in third countries. Its latest sanctions package added 41 vessels and entities supporting the network.
Libya is becoming particularly important to this network as Moscow expands its military infrastructure there.
The Washington-based, offcial “Africa Defense Forum” , citing data from the US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency’s Tearline project, reported that Russia plans to fund infrastructure projects and deploy personnel at six Libyan air bases.
The sites, stretching across central, eastern and southern Libya, are being equipped or refurbished to support Russian aircraft, air defence systems, drones and personnel.

articles.title: Ex-defence minister Fedorov reveals his next steps: venture fund, think tank and lecturing
articles.body:
Ex-defence minister Fedorov reveals his next steps: venture fund, think tank and lecturing
Following his dismissal from government, former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov says he plans to work on a venture fund to attract investment in Ukrainian defence start-ups, set up a think tank and civic initiatives to prepare for a "return to democracy", and lecture at universities.
Source: Fedorov in an interview with 24 Kanal
Details: Fedorov said the plan he brought to the Defence Ministry was called Air-Land-Economy and its focus was protecting Ukraine's airspace, halting the Russian advance, and exhausting Russia's economy.
"I realised that it would be difficult to achieve this plan without effective managers and without reforming the system, so I added another point – Democracy. I'll be working on implementing this plan," he said.
Quote: "This is how I see my path: I need to set up a venture fund that will attract Western funding to invest in Ukrainian start-ups and developers. I have a few priorities – cheap AI-powered missiles… also robotising the line of contact and adding sensors. We need to think about how to remove infantry from the line of contact, because assault troops will be moving into previously enemy-held territory after the robots and drones have gone in… Our task is to saturate the battlefield with sensors that react to enemy infantry movement, triggering immediate reconnaissance and destruction of the enemy.
We started working on this at the Defence Ministry, and I want to continue that work in the private sector. It will be a fund with Western investment that will invest in various projects in Ukraine and bring projects to Ukraine that will help us win."
Details: Fedorov said another of his projects will be a "think tank – an organisation where analysts come up with ways to stop the war and defeat Russia and generate ideas in general. It will be a team of policymakers who develop the rules of the game for the next stages."
The former minister said the think tank's objective will be to "develop a vision for the next stages of the war, stay relevant, and propose to the government what needs to be done to implement these changes".
"There may also be some AI-related start-ups, which will also be connected with defence tech and how to help in the war. This is a key area of activity that I want to develop. I'm confident that a lot of people from all over the world could join this project and support it," he added.
Fedorov also plans to spend some of his time engaging in "civic activities to do with preparing this country for a return to democracy".
"I have a very large team – hundreds of very talented people who are building their lives around the projects I'm going to launch. This is invaluable social capital, and I really want to support these people so that they can fulfil their potential. I think we'll achieve results in these areas," the former minister said.
He also plans to teach "a course on reforms at some universities".
Quote: "Plus I already have projects that I started working on as soon as I left the government. I'm helping several foundations that are working on reforms – how to prepare partner investment and funding for the changes taking place in the government, and how, given the change in strategy, to help the government in the most effective way possible."
